question: Can the firmware AIOTJS system.router/PageNavigator implementation serve as the public native C/Rust router ABI?
prototype_hypothesis: sub_C8E488C is an AIOTJS PageNavigator openPage implementation; sub_C86084C, sub_C8608CC and sub_C8609E4 are JIDL system.router wrappers that obtain the JavaScript app object and dispatch virtual methods or marshal page records.
callsite_evidence: The FLASH_CACHED alias of 'PageNavigator openPage' resolves through pointer storage 0x0C8E4B98 to sub_C8E488C at 0x0C8E4912.
sub_C8E488C also references AIOTJS openPage/page-stack diagnostics and a create-page-error path, and manipulates reference-counted runtime values rather than a plain native route-id stack.
sub_C86084C obtains the 'app' object, checks a virtual function slot and invokes object methods; failure paths reference router_impl.cpp line 336 and trap.
sub_C8608CC references router_impl.cpp line 354, calls a virtual method at slot 24, and allocates/marshals string-bearing return records.
sub_C8609E4 identifies itself as system_router_wrap_getPages and marshals multiple page values for the JIDL feature layer.
control_flow_evidence: These functions belong to the AIOTJS/JIDL runtime and depend on private app objects, virtual tables, allocator-backed strings and runtime exception/trap behavior.
They are not suitable as a stable freestanding C ABI or no_std Rust API, and are rejected as the public router substrate.
The public SDK instead uses an allocator-free bounded semantic route stack; the exact-target backend continues to use the separately recovered native page_goto/page_finish lifecycle in EVID-NAV-001.
Route and UI generations invalidate stale back events, while the public stack stores only application route values and never AIOTJS or firmware page pointers.
ownership_analysis: AIOTJS PageNavigator values are runtime-owned and reference-counted. Their app object, strings and page records cannot safely outlive or bypass the JavaScript runtime. Canopus Router owns only a fixed array of Copy route values; native page descriptors remain target-private.
unsafe_assumptions: The AIOTJS wrapper prototypes are decompiler hypotheses and are intentionally not promoted to callable symbols.
Native page_goto/page_finish remains static-recovered and device-pending as documented by EVID-NAV-001.
No claim is made that the semantic Router reproduces AIOTJS getPages return objects or JavaScript lifecycle hooks.
recommended_probe: Exercise Overview -> Modules -> Detail, replace, pop-to-root, system gesture back, explicit header back, stale double-tap back, backend failure rollback, and 100 repeated navigation cycles on the Manager native pages.

artifacts.role: approved static native page manager path
